# Reference: golden vectors

Byte-exact test vectors for the `terrane-v1` profile. Every vector below was
generated from the rules in the owning file and is normative when a
requirement cites it ([`../00-conventions.md`](../00-conventions.md)).
An implementation MUST reproduce each positive vector exactly and reject
each explicitly negative vector through its format decoder; `gate:golden-vectors`
([`../36-testing-and-conformance.md`](../36-testing-and-conformance.md)
TEST-1) checks every one.

Hex is lowercase. CBOR is shown in diagnostic notation and as the exact
canonical bytes ([`../06-tree-format.md`](../06-tree-format.md) TREE-25).
Identities are BLAKE3-256 over `domain || 0x00 || bytes`
([`../04-content-model.md`](../04-content-model.md) OBJ-2). Signatures use
Ed25519 with the RFC 8032 §7.1 test keys so that any implementation can
regenerate them.

conformance suite.

## Gear table

The FastCDC gear table ([`../05-chunking.md`](../05-chunking.md) CDC-1) is
derived from the profile seed:

```text
bytes   = BLAKE3-XOF( "terrane-gear-v1" || 0x00 || seed, 2048 bytes )
gear[i] = u64le( bytes[8*i .. 8*i + 8] )        for i in 0 .. 256
```

The `cdc-1m` vectors ([`property-registry.md`](property-registry.md)
§chunk profiles) use the all-zero 32-byte seed. A store uses its recorded
seed (CDC-2); these witnesses do not restrict that seed. For the vector seed:

| i | `gear[i]` |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | `0x15f23553a70da356` |
| 1 | `0x9700318b430e40f3` |
| 2 | `0x70cd1174e9697d43` |
| 3 | `0x0026abb73a8487ac` |
| 4 | `0xae9e6f49c0846cb3` |
| 5 | `0xafd4bb99913bf95f` |
| 6 | `0xba377b75cd23033d` |
| 7 | `0xb0cd9e1ce544864c` |

BLAKE3 of the full 2 048-byte table: `22e8d10aa13d65d681fa4ff159d1151c11c90f652bc059d4418c3f463f49b14c`.

For the `cdc-1m` profile, the two level-2 masks derived by CDC-1 are
`0x0000b6db6db70000` up to and including 1 MiB and
`0x0000aab556ab0000` above 1 MiB. Generate a 16,777,216-byte input with
`BLAKE3-XOF("terrane-cdc-boundaries-v1" || 0x00)` and cut it from offset zero
using the all-zero profile seed. The cumulative end offsets, including EOF,
are:

```text
1,053,018   1,336,528   2,676,886   3,833,803   4,242,108
5,460,736   6,765,165   8,343,797   9,434,089  10,501,272
11,945,946  13,357,494  15,153,770  16,005,372  16,777,216
```

`gate:cdc-boundaries` reproduces the stream and checks every offset. The
last offset is the mandatory end-of-file cut.

## Node boundaries

The base threshold `B(S)` for stored encoded size `S` (TREE-22) corresponds
to `1/4096` at `MIN_NODE` = 4 096, rising linearly to `1/256` at 32 768,
constant to `MAX_NODE` = 65 536. For an item with stored encoded length
`L`, the comparison is `h < min(2^32, floor(B(S) * L / 8))`. Hashing uses
the full-key encoding, while `S` and `L` use the stored compressed encoding.

| S (bytes) | base probability | B(S) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4096 | 0.000244141 | 1048576 |
| 8192 | 0.000767299 | 3295524 |
| 12288 | 0.001290458 | 5542473 |
| 16384 | 0.001813616 | 7789421 |
| 20480 | 0.002336775 | 10036370 |
| 24576 | 0.002859933 | 12283318 |
| 28672 | 0.003383092 | 14530267 |
| 32768 | 0.003906250 | 16777216 |
| 49152 | 0.003906250 | 16777216 |
| 65536 | 0.003906250 | 16777216 |

Between table rows `B(S)` is linear in `S` and MUST be computed exactly as
`floor((2^20 + (S - 4096) * (2^24 - 2^20) / 28672))` for
`4096 <= S <= 32768`, using integer arithmetic.

Per-item comparison vectors (the threshold includes the item length):

| S (bytes) | L (bytes) | comparison threshold |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4096 | 8 | 1048576 |
| 8192 | 48 | 19773144 |
| 16384 | 64 | 62315368 |
| 32768 | 128 | 268435456 |
| 65536 | 65536 | 4294967296 |

The final row saturates at `2^32`; it MUST NOT wrap to zero. A node at
`MAX_NODE` closes unconditionally. An item that would exceed the cap is
re-encoded in a new node before the threshold is computed (TREE-22).

## Layout and physical-intent record vectors

These D-80 vectors complete the byte witnesses for D-77's layout version 2
and D-78's protected physical-intent records. Their fields follow
[`terrane-v1.cddl`](terrane-v1.cddl),
[`../13-bucket-layout.md`](../13-bucket-layout.md) and
[`../17-garbage-collection.md`](../17-garbage-collection.md).
Each input model below uses CBOR diagnostic notation. Whitespace inside a
hexadecimal byte string is insignificant. Empty arrays are explicit values;
omitted fields remain absent, rather than null.

Positive vectors fix canonical encoding and decoding. Negative vectors are
canonical CBOR with an invalid field value; their format decoder MUST
reject them. Journal identities and fixed nonce patterns are codec inputs,
not verified filesystem descriptors or secure production randomness.
An Invalidated journal is a valid record that cannot authorize deletion.

The intent binds pack ID `000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f`, cycle 7 and
physical exclusion epoch 2. Its original lease has epoch 3; the current
recovery lease has epoch 4. These distinct epochs do not rewrite the older
physical exclusion. The deletion delay is 60 seconds and its encoded
elapsed lower bound is 60,000,000,000 nanoseconds. Decoding these claims does
not demonstrate that a backend actually waited or checked current roots.
The original authorization is immutable across operation revisions/phases.

The 181-byte pack and its 148-byte detached-index witness bind the exact
artifact versions shown below. The authorization digest is raw BLAKE3 over
its 640 canonical bytes, without an immutable-content domain prefix:

```text
a5802a8ed186b0f68a32c9277ac30f3a39b67941a548d96f2047c082903f6e8c
```

The matching deletion-operation key is:

```text
gc/7/delete/000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f/404142434445464748494a4b4c4d4e4f505152535455565758595a5b5c5d5e5f
```

Every `DeleteOperation` positive vector is decoded against that exact key.
A mismatched cycle, pack ID, nonce, noncanonical decimal or hexadecimal,
suffix or extra segment MUST be rejected. These records do not have
immutable-content descriptors, and a successful codec round trip grants
no publication, reachability, lease, age or deletion authority.

## D-79 publication and original-control format witnesses

D-84 publishes these byte witnesses for the registered D-79
CDDL. They describe represented format inputs only: decoded controls,
bindings and policy rows do not establish native ownership, selected
history, current authorization or a source-preservation fence. Every
record here is non-content-addressed and has no immutable descriptor
or domain-separated identity. Repeated ACL entries preserve order;
the seeded profile intentionally uses a nonzero seed.

Explicitly negative witnesses require format-decoder rejection.
Each named witness supplies its complete diagnostic input and exact
canonical encoding. Compound inputs repeat their full nested records.
All key, digest and registration values are public fixture data.
Raw digest fields use BLAKE3 over the exact represented canonical bytes.
The legacy-lineage and collection-proof examples are structural claims
with incomplete authority evidence; they cannot qualify a native fork
or collection. The remaining current-collection and retirement formats
need their own witnesses before complete TEST-2 coverage is claimed.

## Two-entry pack and detached index

These TEST-1/TEST-2 witnesses use the field tables in 12-pack-format.md. The
fixed pack ID is a byte-format fixture and claims no writer entropy. Bodies
retain physical write order; index records are sorted by content digest. All
integers in the pack and index are little-endian.

```text
pack-id = 000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f
version = 1; flags = 0
physical bodies = [00 || h'68656c6c6f0a', 00 || h'776f726c640a']
plaintext bodies = [h'68656c6c6f0a', h'776f726c640a']
index count = 2; index offset = 38; index CRC32C = a8b09ac2
index records (digest, offset, body length, plaintext length, codec, kind):
(a20aaf262a9604b71e92a33c7f79e430f47128cf4b8a473b8c42c83b273a80cf, 24, 7, 6, 0, 0)
(f8d628d3f53dc54bd01cb5fd43640a894d020dd432d6f2bc69c93700c12de9e5, 31, 7, 6, 0, 0)
dictionary fields = 0; reserved fields = 0
```

rejects the reserved field despite its valid CRC.

Positive container identities hash the complete corresponding bytes with their
registered domain and zero separator. They do not enter tree or commit
identities. Negative wires have no conforming container identity. Structural
decoding does not verify plaintext chunk identities or authorize serving; the
positive tests check those identities separately.

## Collection-record format witnesses

These TEST-1/TEST-2 models transcribe GcLease, GcRoots, GcMark, GcState,
Tombstone and IndexGenerationManifest in terrane-v1.cddl. GC-7 defines the
reconstructed mark hint; GC-30 defines fieldwise proof-context order. These
records have no immutable-content descriptor. Opaque digest fields do not
establish root completeness, verified history, checkpoint authenticity or
effect authority.

Positive format vector.

```text
{1: "collector", 2: 9, 3: 256}
```

## Immutable descriptors and internal-node witnesses

These TEST-2 witnesses cover all eleven registered immutable descriptor
domains and a canonical level-one internal node with two leaf models. The
first leaf closes at a real TREE-21/TREE-22 profile boundary, using a fixed
4,096-byte extended attribute; the second closes as the final tail. The legacy
hello leaf is reproduced separately. Each child count is one; its weight is
the complete leaf's encoded size. Descriptor payloads are reproduced
independently from CDDL and the pack field tables. Deferred filter and memo
payloads are ordinary schema models: descriptor checks do not qualify those
features. Legacy signatures retain their byte-format role and establish no
current authorization or verified history.

## Canonical composition recipe witnesses

These TEST-2 witnesses cover the implemented graft, overlay and merge schemas,
including operand order, replacement, policy order and optional empty domain
records. Positive format inputs carry recipe hashes in the registered memo
domain, without acquiring immutable-content descriptors. The explicit
`terrane-preset-any/v1` trust profile is inert: its decoding cannot authorize
trusted/newer policies. No tree operation, view verification or effective
ownership resolution is performed. Five negative wires require structural
decoder rejection.

## Entry and root-property format witnesses

Twenty-two complete entry models cover all seven kinds, absent and explicit
empty metadata, opaque nonempty metadata, both file content tags, link IDs and
all conflict-base alternatives. Six root leaf models cover absent/empty
properties, every registered property name, nested values and inheritance
wrappers. Three further leaf models retain directory/conditional ancestors and
a complete hard-link set. Entries have no immutable identity; only complete
positive nodes receive a terrane-node-v1 identity. Provenance, selectors,
grants and represented root/content references are inert field data.
Thirty-eight independently constructed negative wires require structural
decoder rejection. These witnesses do not perform tree operations, signing,
verification or policy selection.

## Derived-attribute field model witnesses

These TEST-1/TEST-2 field models cover all eight registered value kinds. Fixed
digest bytes and represented ELF/shebang fields assert no external plaintext
properties. Value fragments have no immutable-content identity. Full records
carry terrane-attr-v1 identities and exact unsigned signature preimages;
optional signatures are fixed opaque bytes, without signing, verification or
authority. Future function version 2 remains format data. Structural negatives
acquire no content identity. These codec comparisons cover DRV-1/2/6/8 format
data only.

## Reproduction

The vectors were produced with the reference BLAKE3 and Ed25519
implementations and a hand-written canonical CBOR encoder. A conformance
suite regenerates them from the same inputs; a mismatch in any byte is a
failure of `gate:golden-vectors`.

The additive D-79 witnesses above use an independent canonical CBOR primitive
encoder and a raw BLAKE3 primitive that hashes supplied bytes without invoking
a Terrane record encoder. The diagnostic models fully describe the inputs;
raw digest fields hash the exact corresponding canonical bytes. Conformance
tests separately construct the represented models and check encoder output,
decoder output, and the explicitly negative decoder inputs. Qualification of
this partial corpus does not qualify the complete `gate:golden-vectors` corpus.

The two-entry pack witnesses use independent little-endian field assembly,
CRC32C and the raw BLAKE3 primitive. Negative inputs preserve the remaining
fields and isolate the stated decoder rejection. Positive tests compare
the complete container bytes and identities, decoded fields and plaintext
chunk identities separately.

The collection-record witnesses use independent CBOR primitives and the GC-7
membership-hint rule. Tests separately construct all positive record models,
compare the complete wire bytes and decoded fields, and reject the five
negative inputs. Their opaque digest fields describe format data rather than
authenticated checkpoints or collection authority.

The descriptor witnesses include complete corresponding immutable payload bytes.
Their tests independently derive all eleven registered identities and compare
encoded descriptors and decoded fields. The internal-node witness uses a real
TREE-21/TREE-22 cut and a final tail; separate tests reconstruct its leaf fields,
exact counts and weights, and reproduce the root with the canonical builder.
Deferred filter and memo payloads qualify descriptor fields only.

The composition witnesses use independent CBOR fields and memo-domain recipe
hashes. Tests separately construct their positive public models, compare
encoded bytes, decoded fields and hashes, and reject the five negative
wire inputs. Empty domain records and the inert trust profile do not
establish ownership or authorize trusted/newer materialization.

The entry/root-property and derived-attribute witnesses use independent CBOR
primitives and complete inert field models. Only whole positive nodes and
attribute records receive registered immutable identities. Attribute preimages
include the registered signature prefix and the complete unsigned record;
present signatures are opaque bytes. Separately constructed owning-codec tests
compare exact bytes and all decoded fields, while primitive negative inputs
isolate structural rejection. These examples do not derive executable metadata,
verify provenance, select policy or perform tree and repository operations.

## Chunk-envelope and merged-shard field witnesses

These TEST-1/2/3 witnesses cover CDC-7/9 envelope fields and PACK-17/18/19/20
shard format only. Plaintext and dictionary identities hash their full bytes
in terrane-chunk-v1, independently of stored envelopes. Primitive RFC 8878
single-segment frames include their content size and only raw blocks; they use
no dictionary references. Core envelope parsing and size checks do not
establish native decompression, dictionary provenance or admission. Ordinary
positive envelopes use cdc-1m's registered 4,194,304-byte maximum, which also
accommodates the dictionary plaintext. Overhead controls instead use a local
structural size oracle with a 100-byte maximum; that context is not a
registered profile. Complete merged shards have terrane-index-v1 identities.
Their embedded content hashes and pack IDs are opaque fixture fields, without
corresponding bodies, entropy, placements, generations or authority. State
bytes represent live, tombstone and quarantine fields without performing those
operations. Negative wires have no identity.

## Permanent-retirement record format witnesses

These TEST-2 witnesses transcribe the disjoint D-82 schemas. They represent
ordinary field models for authorizations, preparations, operations, fences,
ownership selectors and progress records. Digest and embedded-value
relationships are computed from independent CBOR and the raw hash primitive.
No represented nonce, ownership, current placement or elapsed bound
establishes physical permission. The seven negative wires isolate structural
decoder refusals.
